page_title: Building Open-Source Codebase Copilot with Code Execution Layer | E2B

summary.name: Maige
summary.one_liner: Maige is an open-source AI agent that acts as a copilot for GitHub repositories, handling tasks like issue labeling and pull request review, with each repo's agent running in its own E2B sandbox.
use_cases: reviewing pull requests with an AI agent
running tests or reproducing bugs in an isolated sandbox
writing and opening pull requests from AI-generated code
summary.what_it_does: Maige is described as an AI companion for codebase managers and open-source maintainers that can do anything a person could do with the GitHub API, such as labeling issues and reviewing pull requests. Maintainers connect it to a repository and write custom natural-language rules that trigger agent actions on events like new issues or comments. Each connected repository gets its own E2B sandbox where the repo is cloned, dependencies are installed, and the agent runs shell commands, tests, or code changes, then commits and opens a pull request as a bot user. The stack uses a serverless function, OpenAI embeddings with GPT-4 Turbo, a Weaviate vector database on Railway, and PlanetScale MySQL, and it is designed to be self-hostable.
notable: Each repository gets its own isolated E2B sandbox for the agent
Open-source and self-hostable to avoid vendor lock-in
Custom rules written in natural language trigger agent actions on GitHub events
Installed on more than 2,000 GitHub repos, per the page
caveats: Still in alpha stage as of the interview
AI agents can get stuck in loops or give up tasks, and generated code edits are unreliable according to the founder
Requires granting GitHub permissions such as opening pull requests
